title: The undying pair: Butcher Ghoul + Geralf's Messenger under Yawgmoth — is the loop unbounded, and what does each opponent lose per cycle?

you: Butcher Ghoul (1/1 printed; carries ONE +1/+1 counter from a previous undying return, so it is currently 2/2)
Geralf's Messenger (3/2) — already sacrificed to pay the cost of the ability now on the stack

scenario.mana_available: {0} (Yawgmoth's ability costs no mana to activate)

stack.item: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician's activated ability (its cost is already paid: 1 life was paid and Geralf's Messenger was sacrificed) — targeting Butcher Ghoul for the -1/-1 counter; will also draw a card
Geralf's Messenger's undying trigger (it died with no +1/+1 counters on it)
Zulaport Cutthroat's triggered ability (Geralf's Messenger, a creature you control, died) — each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life

extras.note_for_the_resolver: Both triggers are controlled by the same player, who chose to put the Zulaport Cutthroat trigger on top. The deck's goldfish declaration (KILL F) currently labels this two-undying loop 'unbounded' — the point of this artifact is to verify or refute that word against the rules. Note that Yawgmoth's draw is mandatory ('and draw a card'), and note what Geralf's Messenger does when it re-enters. Sibling stack 010 settled the counter-annihilation SBA for the Mikaeus variant; this scenario is the tutor-free two-undying version the community lists treat as the deck's signature line.
assumptions: Your library has roughly 55 cards remaining.
No opponent has a response; resolve in a vacuum.

scenario.question: Resolve this stack. Then: can the pilot repeat the loop — alternating Yawgmoth activations that sacrifice whichever undying creature is counter-free while stripping the other's +1/+1 counter — indefinitely, or is 'unbounded' the wrong word? State precisely what bounds the loop, and how much life each opponent loses per full two-activation cycle.

steps.action: Resolve the top object: Zulaport Cutthroat's triggered ability (Geralf's Messenger, a creature you control, died).
steps.effect: Each of the three opponents loses 1 life (40 -> 39, 40 -> 39, 40 -> 39) and you gain 1 life (20 -> 21; the 1 life for Yawgmoth's activation cost was already paid, per the scenario's stated life totals). Pod total so far: 3 life.

citations.quote: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.

steps.action: Resolve the next object: Geralf's Messenger's undying trigger. Check its intervening 'if' clause on resolution.
steps.effect: The condition — it had no +1/+1 counters on it when it died — was true at the trigger event and remains true on resolution, so the ability resolves: Geralf's Messenger returns from your graveyard to the battlefield under your control with a +1/+1 counter on it. Its 'enters tapped' replacement effect applies, so it enters tapped. Its enters-the-battlefield ability triggers: 'When this creature enters, target opponent loses 2 life.'

citations.quote: Undying is a triggered ability. “Undying” means “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner’s control with a +1/+1 counter on it.”
If the ability triggers, it checks the stated condition again as it resolves. If the condition isn’t true at that time, the ability is removed from the stack and does nothing.
Continuous effects that read “[This permanent] enters . . .” or “[Objects] enter [the battlefield] . . .” are replacement effects.
Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield.

steps.action: Before any player receives priority, the Messenger's enters trigger is put on the stack — above Yawgmoth's still-pending activated ability. You choose a target: opponent 1.
steps.effect: The stack is now (top to bottom): Messenger's ETB trigger targeting opponent 1; Yawgmoth's activated ability targeting Butcher Ghoul.

citations.quote: Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
Then triggered abilities are put on the stack (see rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities”).

steps.effect: Opponent 1 loses 2 life (39 -> 37). Opponents now at 37 / 39 / 39.

citations.quote: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.

steps.action: Resolve Yawgmoth, Thran Physician's activated ability (bottom of the original stack). Target check first.
steps.effect: Butcher Ghoul is still on the battlefield and is a legal target. A -1/-1 counter is put on it — it now has one +1/+1 counter and one -1/-1 counter — and you draw a card. The draw is mandatory ('and draw a card', no 'may'). Library ~55 -> ~54.

citations.quote: If the spell or ability specifies targets, it checks whether the targets are still legal.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.

steps.action: State-based actions are checked before any player receives priority: counter annihilation on Butcher Ghoul.
steps.effect: N=1: one +1/+1 counter and one -1/-1 counter are removed from Butcher Ghoul. It is a 1/1 with NO counters — exactly the state undying needs for its next death. No player is at 0 or less life; no creature has lethal damage or 0 toughness. The stack is empty. Board: Yawgmoth, Butcher Ghoul (1/1, counter-free), Zulaport Cutthroat, Geralf's Messenger (tapped, one +1/+1 counter). You 21; opponents 37/39/39.

citations.quote: If a permanent has both a +1/+1 counter and a -1/-1 counter on it, N +1/+1 and N -1/-1 counters are removed from it, where N is the smaller of the number of +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters on it.

Each time a player would get priority, the game first performs all applicable state-based actions as a single event (see rule 704, “State-Based Actions”), then repeats this process until no state-based actions are performed.

steps.action: LOOP ANALYSIS — the mirrored second activation. Pay 1 life, sacrifice Butcher Ghoul (now counter-free), targeting Geralf's Messenger with the -1/-1 counter.
steps.effect: Butcher Ghoul died with no +1/+1 counters, so undying triggers and returns it with a +1/+1 counter; Zulaport Cutthroat triggers again (each opponent loses 1, you gain 1); the -1/-1 counter annihilates the Messenger's +1/+1 counter via the same state-based action, leaving the Messenger counter-free for the next Messenger-sacrifice; you draw a second card. The counter-stripping is what keeps the loop alive: a creature that dies WITH a +1/+1 counter fails undying's intervening 'if' and never triggers at all. Butcher Ghoul has no enters trigger, so the Ghoul half of the cycle drains only via Zulaport. PER FULL TWO-ACTIVATION CYCLE: each opponent loses 2 (Zulaport, one per death); the opponent targeted by the Messenger's enters trigger loses 2 more (so 4 total for that seat); pod total 8 (6 Zulaport + 2 Messenger). You pay 2 life and gain 2 from Zulaport — net 0 — and draw 2 cards.

citations.quote: “Undying” means “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner’s control with a +1/+1 counter on it.”
When the trigger event occurs, the ability checks whether the stated condition is true. The ability triggers only if it is; otherwise it does nothing.
If a permanent has both a +1/+1 counter and a -1/-1 counter on it, N +1/+1 and N -1/-1 counters are removed from it, where N is the smaller of the number of +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters on it.

steps.effect: 'Unbounded' is REFUTED. Yawgmoth's draw is not optional: the resolving ability's instructions must be followed, and 'and draw a card' contains no 'may'. Every activation therefore consumes one library card. With ~55 cards in the library, the pilot can make at most ~55 activations (including the one just resolved) — about 27 full two-activation cycles — before the library is empty; the next mandatory draw after that would be from an empty library, and the pilot loses the game as a state-based action. The loop is BOUNDED BY LIBRARY SIZE, not by life (net 0 per cycle) or by bodies (the two undying creatures recycle indefinitely in principle). It is also not a rules-mandated loop: each iteration begins with a discretionary activation, so the pilot simply stops before the last safe draw — but a set of actions that cannot be 'repeated indefinitely' is, by the CR's own definition of a loop, not unbounded.

citations.quote: The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.
A player who attempts to draw a card from a library with no cards in it loses the game the next time a player would receive priority. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)
If a player attempted to draw a card from a library with no cards in it since the last time state-based actions were checked, that player loses the game.
Occasionally the game gets into a state in which a set of actions could be repeated indefinitely (thus creating a “loop”).

steps.action: LETHALITY WITHIN THE BOUND — does KILL F still kill?
steps.effect: Yes, comfortably. Over n activations each opponent loses n life to Zulaport (one death per activation) plus 2 per Messenger enters-trigger aimed at them; the Messenger trigger fires on every odd-numbered activation (ceil(n/2) times). At n = 30 activations (15 cycles), Zulaport alone deals 30 to each seat and the 15 Messenger triggers, spread 5/5/5, add 10 more — 40 per opponent, exactly lethal from 40, with each opponent losing the game as a state-based action at 0 or less life. 30 activations cost 30 draws against a ~55-card library, leaving ~25 cards of margin. Correct label for KILL F: not 'unbounded' but 'library-bounded (~55 iterations available), lethal to the pod in ~30'.

citations.quote: If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.

final_state.summary: Stack empty after the presented stack resolves: opponents at 37/39/39, you at 21, library ~54, board Yawgmoth + Butcher Ghoul (1/1, counter-free) + Zulaport Cutthroat + Geralf's Messenger (tapped, one +1/+1 counter) — the loop is primed for the mirrored Ghoul-sacrifice activation. VERDICT: 'unbounded' is the wrong word. The loop is bounded by the library, because Yawgmoth's draw is mandatory: ~55 activations maximum (~27 full cycles), after which the next mandatory draw loses the game (121.4 / 704.5b). Per full two-activation cycle: each opponent loses 2 (Zulaport), the Messenger-targeted opponent loses 4, pod total 8, you net 0 life and draw 2. The bound does not save the table: ~30 activations kill all three opponents from 40, ~25 draws inside the bound.

battlefield: Geralf's Messenger (3/2 base, tapped, one +1/+1 counter)

opponents.note: targeted by Geralf's Messenger's enters trigger

findings.note: Top object (Zulaport trigger, last-added per the scenario's stated ordering choice) resolves first.

Each-opponent drain applied per seat (40->39 x3) AND pod total (3) stated separately; matches scenario-facts drain arithmetic and Zulaport's oracle text ('each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life').
Undying return with a +1/+1 counter under owner's control; owner is the pilot, so 'under your control' is correct here.

Intervening-if re-check on resolution handled; the condition is past-tense (had no +1/+1 counters when it died), so it remains true. Full rule text confirms both the trigger-time and resolution-time checks.
'This creature enters tapped' is a replacement effect; Messenger enters tapped. Matches oracle text.
ETB trigger ('When this creature enters, target opponent loses 2 life') fires on the undying return.
Trigger goes on the stack at next-priority, above the still-pending Yawgmoth ability; target (a player) chosen as it is put on the stack.
Quote is the trigger-placement sentence of 117.5; full rule also mandates SBAs first, which are vacuous at this point (nothing applies).
ETB trigger is the top object and resolves. Target legality re-check (608.2b) is not cited here but is trivially satisfied: opponent 1 is still in the game, resolving in a vacuum.
Target opponent loses 2 (39->37). Correctly single-seat, not each-opponent — the per-seat/pod distinction is maintained.

Explicit target legality re-check; Butcher Ghoul still on the battlefield. (Yawgmoth's ability is 'up to one target creature' — a target was chosen and remains legal, so the distinction does not matter here.)
Instructions in order: counter, then mandatory draw ('and draw a card', no 'may' — verified against oracle text). SBAs correctly deferred to after resolution.
N=1 annihilation leaves Butcher Ghoul 1/1 with zero counters — re-armed for undying. Consistent with sibling 010's settled mechanism (referenced as precedent only; no figures quoted across boards).
SBAs performed before priority, repeated until none apply; the other SBA checks (life, lethal damage, 0 toughness) correctly reported vacuous.

Mirrored half-cycle: Ghoul dies counter-free, returns with a counter; Ghoul has no ETB so its half drains via Zulaport only. Cycle arithmetic verified by independent simulation: each opponent -2/cycle, Messenger-targeted seat -4, pod 8 (6 Zulaport + 2 Messenger), pilot net 0 life, 2 draws.

Correctly states that a creature dying WITH a +1/+1 counter fails the intervening if at trigger time and the ability never triggers — this is why the counter-stripping sustains the loop. The two death triggers of the mirrored activation are the same controller's; ordering is unstated but every claimed total is order-invariant.
The -1/-1 on Messenger annihilates its +1/+1 at the next SBA check, leaving it counter-free for the next Messenger sacrifice.
The mandatory-draw premise of the bound: resolving ability's instructions must be followed.
Drawing from an empty library loses the game via SBA. Bound arithmetic checks: 55-card library = ~55 activations max (draw 55 empties it; draw 56 loses), ~27 full cycles.
The SBA form of the empty-library loss; consistent with 121.4.
Used definitionally: the CR's loop concept is a set of actions repeatable indefinitely; this set is not (library-bounded), so 'unbounded' is refuted. Fair use of the full rule's context.

Lethality arithmetic verified by independent simulation: 30 activations, Messenger ETB on each odd activation (15 total) spread 5/5/5, leaves all three seats at exactly 0 (40 = 30 Zulaport + 10 Messenger each) with no seat reaching 0 before activation 30; library margin 25 of 55. Per-seat and pod figures never conflated.
